alt: Theme 2, اردو بولنے والی دُنیا میں تمدن اور فنونِ لطیفہ (Art and culture in the Urdu-speaking world), has three sub-themes: folklore and tradition (لوک رسوم و روایت), popular culture (مقبول کلچر) and the media (میڈیا), the research subject.
caption: Three sub-themes; the media is the research subject.

alt: For Themes 1, 3 and 4 research must concern Pakistan; for Theme 2 it may concern Pakistan or one area of India where Urdu is an official language, but only one country or area.
caption: Theme 2 allows Pakistan or one Urdu-official area of India, never both.

after: ## Sub-theme 2.1: folklore and tradition (لوک رسوم و روایت)
alt: Heritage (وراثت) at the centre of four strands: oral tradition (زبانی روایت), folk tales and poetry such as Heer and Ranjha (لوک کہانی), festivals and customs such as melas (میلہ), and performance traditions including the mushaira (مشاعرہ), plus preservation and change.
caption: Oral tradition, tales, festivals and performance, and how they survive or change.

alt: Popular-culture vocabulary (ڈراما, فلم, موسیقی, کھیل, فیشن, نوجوان, رجحان) and the debate it feeds: regional entertainment and international styles mix, and you can argue whether this enriches or dilutes local culture.
caption: Use popular culture to argue whether global influence enriches or dilutes.

alt: Five areas for media research with Urdu terms: print and broadcast (اخبار, رسالہ, نشریات), online and social media (سوشل میڈیا, خبر), influence (اثر, اشتہار), freedom and responsibility (آزادیٔ اظہار), and how Urdu’s register changes across news, drama and advertising.
caption: Cover each area with two viewpoints and sources you have checked.

after: ## Worked example: a model paragraph, with annotation
alt: The four sentences of the model paragraph on folk traditions: a general statement with a feminine plural verb, an example with the passive پیش کی جاتی ہیں, an opinion with اگر ... تو, and a recommendation introduced by اس لیے.
caption: Statement, example, conditional opinion and recommendation.
